newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates rise to 24.375 pct, trade active.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates rise to 24.375 pct, trade active.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank rates closed up at 24.375 percent in active trade on Wednesday with dealers citing tax payments and the closing of dollar futures contracts this week as the main factors.
"The takers were very active because the tax payment is closing on the 20th and there is the position closing for the September futures contract," said Sandor Szatmari of Unicbank.
"The banks have to buy on the interbank spot market and they already started last week...so that can be a strong reason why there was a definite shortage on the market," he added.
The rate was up from Tuesday's close of 23.50.

Traders said the National Bank of Hungary's modest cut on Monday in the repo rate was having little dampening effect on rates, with some saying they expected the interbank rate to remain above 24 percent for the remainder of the week.
The NBH cut the overnight and one-week repo rates to 28.75 percent each and reduced its one-week reverse repo to 22.75 percent and its one-month reverse repo to 23.25 percent.

"Before the repo rate cut, which was well known, everybody bought securities because everybody expected a rate lowering and that's why nobody has much money," said Marton Kerekes of Europai Kereskedelmi Bank, explaining demand in the market.
